A11yCaret.description: The accessibility caret: a position in a node's text.

offset.description: The position, in UTF-16 code units into the node's text.

A11yChange.description: One change to the accessibility tree.

node.description: The new version of the node, children included.

A11yChangeKind.description: The kind of an accessibility change.

oneOf.description: The node replaces the node with the same `id`.

A11yNode.description: A node of the accessibility tree.

chars.description: The box of every character of `text`, on the page of `bounds`.

child_count.description: The number of the node's children, on a node that holds fewer than all of them (spec §14.7): the shell loads the rest with `query.a11y` and a `children` range.

children.description: The node's children, in reading order.

children_start.description: The index of the first child that the node holds, on a node that holds some but not all of its children; they are always one unbroken run.

dir.description: The node's direction, on a node that sets it; its descendants inherit it unless they set their own. The document node always has it.

editable.description: Whether the user can edit the node's text.

id.description: The node's identifier, stable for its lifetime.

lang.description: The node's language, as a BCP 47 tag, on a node that sets it; its descendants inherit it unless they set their own (spec §14.7). The document node always has it.

line_starts.description: The offsets in `text` at which its lines start, as laid out, from 0 in increasing order; on every node that holds text.

name.description: An accessible name where the content does not provide one.

runs.description: The parts of the node's own text whose language or direction differs from the node's, in order and without overlapping.

text.description: The node's own text, on nodes that hold text.

A11yRole.description: The role of an accessibility node.

oneOf.description: A header cell of a column.

A11ySelection.description: A selected range of text (spec §14.7): from `anchor`, the end that stays when the selection is extended, to `focus`, where the caret is.

focus.description: Where the selection ends, and the caret is.

selection.description: The document's selection (spec §14.7): empty when nothing is selected, so that a caret alone is no selection. The engine always sends it; an engine of protocol v1 from before CORE-014 does not.
The document's selection (spec §14.7): empty when nothing is selected. The engine always sends it; an engine of protocol v1 from before CORE-014 does not.

anyOf.description: A code or a short identifier, such as a message type.

ArgValue.description: One value in the `args` of an error or warning: only codes and numbers, never document content (spec §12).

BlobRef.description: A blob: bulk bytes kept outside the JSON (spec §3). On the C interface, its identifier, a positive integer; on the web, the bytes themselves as an `ArrayBuffer` (spec §3.2).

accessibility.description: Whether the shell bridges the accessibility tree to the platform.

clipboard_formats.description: The clipboard formats the shell can exchange, as MIME types.

ime.description: Whether the shell forwards input-method composition.

visible.description: Whether the shell should show it.

end.description: The code unit after the character.

rect.description: The character's box, in page coordinates.

start.description: The character's first UTF-16 code unit in the node's text.

ChildRange.description: A range of a node's children: at most `count` of them, from index `start` on.

count.description: The most children to return; at least 1.

start.description: The index of the first child, counting from 0.

ClipboardCopy.description: `clipboard.copy`: asks for the selection's content, for the platform's copy or cut action (spec §14.5).

cut.description: Whether to cut: the engine also deletes the selection where the document is editable.

ClipboardItem.description: One format of a clipboard's content, as raw bytes (spec §14.5).

blob.description: The bytes; text formats as UTF-8.

mime.description: The format, as a MIME type such as `text/plain`.

ClipboardItems.description: The reply to `clipboard.copy`: the selection in every format the engine writes, which the shell writes to the platform's clipboard as raw bytes; empty when nothing is selected.

items.description: The formats, each as a blob that the shell releases.

CompositionPhase.description: The phase of an input method composition.

oneOf.description: A composition begins at the caret.
The composition's text or selection changed.
The composition ends; its text is discarded (committed text arrives as `input.text`).

DocOpen.description: `doc.open`: opens a document from a blob.

blob.description: The document's bytes. Until real documents can be opened, the engine opens the mock document whatever they contain.

file_name_hint.description: The file name, for format detection and display only; never logged.

format_hint.description: The format, if the shell knows it, such as `docx`.

fonts.description: Fonts the document asks for that are missing.

page_count_estimate.description: How many pages the document is expected to have.

revision.description: The document's render revision (spec §14.6): a positive integer below 2⁵³ that grows with every change to what any of the document's tiles shows.

warnings.description: Problems found while opening, as Fluent messages.

DocumentKey.description: A key that the engine handles in the document area, with any modifiers.

key.description: The key, as the DOM's `KeyboardEvent.key` names it.

Empty.description: A payload without fields: the payload of requests that need none, and the reply to requests that only succeed or fail.

EngineError.description: `engine.error`: an error without a request to answer, or a panic (spec §12).

args.description: Codes and numbers that explain the error; never document content.

message_id.description: A Fluent message identifier, for people.

recoverable.description: `true`: the engine kept its state. `false`: it discarded its session; `restart` says what follows.

restart.description: On every `engine.error` with `recoverable: false`, added by the engine's binding (spec §14.2): `{ number, limit }` while the restart allowance lasts, and the shell starts restart `number` of `limit` with `hello`; `null` when it is used up, and the engine has stopped and answers nothing more. Absent on errors the engine recovered from.

oneOf.description: Not a JSON object of the envelope's shape, or not UTF-8.
A message other than `hello` whose `v` is not the protocol version, or a `hello` that offers no common version.
A message other than `hello` before the handshake.
An unknown message type, or one this engine does not implement.
The payload does not have the message's shape, or a value is out of range.
An unknown document, blob, page or node.
The recording comes from another engine version, protocol version or layout epoch.
`diag.panic` without its test switch, or `diag.replay` while recording.
The engine panicked while handling the message.
Any other failure inside the engine.

ErrorInfo.description: The error of a failed reply (spec §4).

args.description: Codes and numbers that explain the error; never document content.

message_id.description: A Fluent message identifier, for people.

Event.description: A message the engine sends without being asked (spec §4).

seq.description: Increases by one with every event an engine instance sends.

FontReport.description: Fonts a document asks for that the engine does not have.

machine_dependent.description: Whether the layout depends on a font found only among the user's installed fonts (ADR-0004 §3).

Hello.description: `hello`: the shell starts a session (spec §5, §14.1). The engine reads it whatever its envelope's `v`.

locale.description: The interface language, as a BCP 47 tag.

protocol_versions.description: The protocol versions the shell speaks; must contain 1, the only version this engine speaks.

theme.description: The interface theme, such as `light` or `dark`.

Hit.description: The text position at a point (spec §14.4).

caret.description: The caret position nearest to the point: the offset at the nearer edge, in the line's visual order, of the character under or beside the point, so that in right-to-left text the right half of a character gives the offset before it.

character.description: The offset of the character whose box holds the point, or `null` when the point lies on no character's box.

node.description: The accessibility node whose text the offsets are in.

hit.description: What lies at the point, or `null` when the point is on no page.

ImageBitmapRef.description: An `ImageBitmap` transferred from the web worker (spec §3.2); only in the TypeScript declarations.

selection.description: The input method's caret or selection within `text`.

code.description: The physical key, as the DOM's `KeyboardEvent.code`, such as `KeyA`.

composing.description: Whether an input method composition owns the key; the engine then ignores it.

key.description: The key's meaning, as the DOM's `KeyboardEvent.key`, such as `Backspace` or `ArrowLeft`.

repeat.description: Whether the key repeats because it is held down.

InputPaste.description: `input.paste`: the content of the platform's clipboard, which the engine inserts at the selection (spec §14.5).

items.description: The clipboard's bytes in every format that both the shell and the engine list. The engine inserts the richest format it reads and ignores the others: it keeps only the first item of each format of `welcome.clipboard_formats`, and skips every other item without storing it.

InputPointer.description: `input.pointer`: a mouse, pen or touch event.

button.description: The button, numbered as the DOM's `button`: 0 is the primary button.

clicks.description: The click count: 2 for a double click.

x.description: The horizontal position, in device-independent pixels from the view origin.

y.description: The vertical position, in device-independent pixels from the view origin.

InputSelect.description: `input.select`: sets the selection, which is a caret where `anchor` and `focus` are equal (spec §14.4). The engine answers with `overlay.update` and `a11y.update` when the selection changes. A node that does not exist is `not_found`; a node that is not editable, or an offset beyond its node's text or inside a surrogate pair, is `invalid_request`.

anchor.description: Where the selection starts: the end that stays when it is extended.

focus.description: Where the selection ends: the end that moves, and where the caret is.

replace.description: The range of a node's text that `text` replaces; the caret ends after the new text (spec §14.4). A node that does not exist is `not_found`; a node that is not editable, a range outside its text or backwards, or an end inside a surrogate pair is `invalid_request`.

text.description: The text. Without `replace`, it replaces the selection, or is inserted at the caret when nothing is selected; an active composition ends, and the text takes its place.

KeyBinding.description: A key binding of a command (spec §14.3): a key, named by `key` or by `code`, with all four modifiers.

code.description: The physical key as the DOM's `KeyboardEvent.code` names it, such as `KeyA`, for a binding that follows a key's position rather than its character.

key.description: The key as the DOM's `KeyboardEvent.key` names it: a lower-case letter, a digit, a punctuation character, or a name such as `F7`. Exactly one of `key` and `code` is given.

label.description: The binding as the platform writes it, such as `Ctrl+B` or `⌘B`.

Modifiers.description: The modifier keys held during an input event.

meta.description: Meta (Command on macOS, the Windows key on Windows).

OverlayUpdate.description: `overlay.update`: what the shell draws over the tiles (spec §6.3).

caret.description: The caret, or `null` when there is none.

highlights.description: Find highlights (Phase 2); always empty so far.

remote.description: Other people's cursors (Phase 3); always empty so far.

revision.description: The render revision that the rectangles belong to (spec §14.6).

section.description: The index of the page's section.

x.description: The page's left edge in view space.

y.description: The page's top edge in view space.

PageRect.description: A rectangle on a page, in that page's coordinates.

rect.description: The rectangle, in BLU from the page's top-left corner.

Platform.description: The operating system whose keyboard conventions apply (spec §14.1). The engine uses it only to resolve the UI manifest's key bindings (spec §14.3); nothing that affects layout or rendering depends on it (ADR-0004).

oneOf.description: Any other system, and any value the engine does not know; Ctrl stays Ctrl.
A finger on a touch screen.

children.description: A range of the node's children to load, for a node that a tree gave with `child_count` (spec §14.7). The answer holds the node with as many of these children as fit, each with as much of its own subtree as fits, and at least one whenever the node has a child at `start`.

node.description: The node whose subtree to return; the whole document when omitted.

QueryHit.description: `query.hit`: asks which text position lies at a point (spec §14.4).

x.description: The horizontal position, in device-independent pixels from the view origin, as for `input.pointer`.

y.description: The vertical position, in device-independent pixels from the view origin.

blob.description: The recording (spec §10), as a blob that the shell releases.

truncated.description: Whether a limit stopped the recording early.

Rect.description: A rectangle in BLU (1/25,400 point, ADR-0005).

RenderInvalidate.description: `render.invalidate`: parts of pages whose tiles the shell must request again (spec §14.6). A shell keeps a tile while no invalidation with a higher revision covers it.

regions.description: The regions changed since the previous revision, in page coordinates.

revision.description: The document's render revision after the change.

RenderTile.description: `render.tile`: asks for the pixels of part of a page (spec §6.4).

device_scale.description: Physical pixels per device-independent pixel, a hint for later rasterizers; it does not change the pixels.

height.description: The tile's height in pixels, 1 to 4,096.

mode.description: The rasterizer to use (ADR-0011 §3); both give the same pixels until the real rasterizers exist.

rect.description: The part of the page, in page coordinates.

width.description: The tile's width in pixels, 1 to 4,096.

zoom.description: The zoom factor, a hint for later rasterizers; it does not change the pixels.

RenderTileReply.description: The reply to `render.tile` in the message form, on the C interface.

blob.description: The pixels, premultiplied RGBA8, rows from top to bottom, as a blob that the shell releases.

hash.description: The digest of the pixels, `fnv1a64:` and 16 hexadecimal digits (spec §10).

revision.description: The render revision that the tile shows (spec §14.6).

stride.description: Bytes from the start of one row to the next: 4 × width.

RenderTileWebReply.description: The reply to `render.tile` as the web worker host delivers it (spec §3.2): the pixels as an `ImageBitmap`. This type exists for the TypeScript declarations; no JSON has this shape.

hash.description: The digest of the engine's premultiplied pixels (spec §10).

revision.description: The render revision that the tile shows (spec §14.6).

first_difference.description: The index of the first entry that did not, or `null`.

identical.description: Whether every entry produced exactly what it produced when it was recorded.

tiles.description: Every tile rendered during the replay.

ReplayTile.description: A tile rendered during a replay.

entry.description: The index of the entry that rendered it.

Reply.description: The engine's reply to a request with an `id` (spec §4).

ReplyOk.description: A successful reply. Its payload has the reply type that `x-bayan-messages` lists for the request.

type.description: The reply's name, where the specification gives one (`welcome`, `doc.opened`).

Request.description: A message from the shell to the engine (spec §4). Without `id`, the engine sends no reply.

ReservedKey.description: A press that the shell keeps (spec §14.3): a key, named by `key` or by `code`, with only the modifiers that matter; one that it leaves out matches either state.

code.description: The physical key as the DOM's `KeyboardEvent.code` names it.

key.description: The key as the DOM's `KeyboardEvent.key` names it. Exactly one of `key` and `code` is given.

Restart.description: A restart that the restart allowance grants (spec §14.2).

limit.description: How many restarts the allowance grants within ten minutes: 3.

number.description: Which restart this is within the last ten minutes, from 1 to `limit`.

Runtime.description: Whether the shell runs natively or in a browser (spec §14.1), which keeps keys that a native app does not (spec §14.3).

oneOf.description: A web page in a browser.
A native application, and any value the engine does not know.

platform.description: The operating system whose keyboard conventions apply (spec §14.1); a browser shell names the system it runs on, as far as the browser tells it. A missing or unknown value counts as `other`.

runtime.description: Whether the shell runs natively or in a browser (spec §14.1). A missing or unknown value counts as `native`.

TextPosition.description: A position in the text of an accessibility node (spec §14.4): the node, and an offset in UTF-16 code units into its `text`, never inside a surrogate pair.

offset.description: The offset, in UTF-16 code units into the node's text.

TextRange.description: A range of UTF-16 code units.

end.description: The code unit after the last one; equal to `start` for an empty range (a caret).

TextReplace.description: The range of a node's text that `input.text` replaces (spec §14.4), in UTF-16 code units of the node's text as the engine last sent it.

end.description: The code unit after the range; equal to `start` to insert without replacing.

node.description: The accessibility node whose text it is.

start.description: The first code unit of the range.

TextRun.description: A part of a node's own text whose language or direction differs from the node's (spec §14.7).

dir.description: The part's direction, where it differs from the node's.

end.description: The code unit after the part.

lang.description: The part's language, as a BCP 47 tag, where it differs from the node's.

start.description: The first UTF-16 code unit of the part.

UiCommand.description: A command of the UI manifest.

bindings.description: Its key bindings, resolved for the session's platform and runtime (spec §14.3).

shell_action.description: For a command that the shell carries out itself through the platform, such as the clipboard's: `copy`, `cut` or `paste` in v1. A shell that meets a value it does not know neither sends the command's keys nor offers the command (spec §14.3).

UiGroup.description: A group of a ribbon tab.

commands.description: The identifiers of its commands, in order.

UiKeys.description: The key data of the UI manifest (spec §14.3).

document.description: The keys that the engine handles in the document area with any modifiers.

reserved.description: The presses that the shell keeps for itself, the operating system or the browser, even where a binding or a document key matches them.

UiManifest.description: The UI manifest: a stub until ADR-0019's manifest (spec §6.8), with its key data resolved for the session's platform and runtime (spec §14.3).

keys.description: The keys that the engine handles in the document area, and those that the shell keeps (spec §14.3).

manifest_version.description: The stub manifest's format version: 0, until ADR-0019's manifest.

locale.description: The language of the strings, as a BCP 47 tag.

page_count_estimate.description: How many pages the document is expected to have.

pages_laid_out.description: The number of pages laid out so far.

oneOf.description: Print layout: pages as they print.

ViewPages.description: `view.pages`: the document's pages and where they sit in view space (spec §7).

ViewSet.description: `view.set`: tells the engine what the shell shows.

show_formatting_marks.description: Whether to show paragraph marks and other formatting marks.

viewport.description: The visible part of the page area, in device-independent pixels from the view origin.

zoom.description: The zoom factor: 1 shows a document at its real size.

Warning.description: A problem found while opening a document.

args.description: Codes and numbers for the message.

clipboard_formats.description: The clipboard formats that the engine reads and writes, as MIME types, preferred first (spec §14.5): `text/plain`. The engine always sends it; an engine of protocol v1 from before CORE-014 does not, and reads and writes no clipboard formats.

engine_version.description: The core's version as Semantic Versioning 2.0 writes it, at most 64 ASCII characters (spec §14.1).

features.description: What this engine offers, such as `mock_document`.

protocol_version.description: The protocol version of the session: 1.

description: Every message of engine protocol v1 (BayanDocs docs repository, specs/engine-protocol.md), generated from the engine's Rust types. A message is a request, a reply or an event.
